title: Usage Insights: CSV export format spec (working)
body:
Doc status: working spec. Expect churn during beta as we reconcile totals vs Billing and tighten route/model bucketing rules.

Owner: Dylan (Console & Tooling)
Primary reviewers: Nadia (cost attribution), Logan (telemetry/warehouse), Rishi (finance reporting), Marcus/Naomi (security & audit requirements)

---

1) Goal / non-goals

Goal
- Define a stable, machine-ingestable CSV export format for Usage Insights.
- CSV should support:
  - Engineering: cost + usage by route + model, drillable in BI tools
  - Finance/FinOps: reconciliation vs invoice/billing exports, chargeback by project/workspace
  - Support: debugging discrepancies and explaining “what changed” drivers

Non-goals (v1)
- Scheduled recurring delivery (email/S3) (tracked separately)
- Fully customer-defined custom dimensions
- Perfect parity with every internal raw telemetry field (export is aggregated)

---

2) Export types (files)

We will support two export “shapes” initially.

A) Breakdown export (primary)
- One row per aggregation bucket (time bucket) per dimension set.
- Typical: hourly or daily buckets (depending on time range).

B) Top drivers export (optional / later)
- One row per driver card output with explainability text.
- Not required for beta; included here only for forward compatibility notes.

This document focuses on (A).

---

3) File format

Encoding
- UTF-8

Delimiter
- Comma (,)

Line endings
- LF (\n)

Quoting
- RFC 4180 compatible.
- Fields containing comma, quote, or newline MUST be quoted with double quotes.
- Double quotes inside quoted fields escaped as "".

Header row
- Required. Exact column names as specified below.

Null / missing values
- Empty cell (e.g., ,,)
- Do NOT emit literal "null".

Booleans
- "true" / "false" (lowercase)

---

4) Naming + ordering of columns

Column ordering is part of the contract.
- We should keep stable ordering so spreadsheets/BI imports don’t break.
- New columns appended to end only (never inserted in the middle) unless we version the export.

Versioning
- export_schema_version column included.
- v1 = first public beta shape.

---

5) Core breakdown CSV columns (v1)

NOTE: All currency amounts are DECIMAL rendered as string (not scientific notation). Tokens/requests are integers.

A) Export metadata
1. export_schema_version
   - Example: "1"

2. export_generated_at
   - ISO-8601 UTC timestamp.
   - Example: "2026-02-12T18:44:09Z"

3. export_time_zone
   - Time zone used to compute bucket boundaries.
   - Example: "UTC" (beta default)

4. export_query_time_range_start
   - ISO-8601 timestamp at start (inclusive)

5. export_query_time_range_end
   - ISO-8601 timestamp at end (exclusive)

6. export_filters
   - Human-readable summary string (for quick audit).
   - Example: "workspace=ws_9f2…; project=all; env=prod; region=all; deployment_mode=all; group_by=route,model; bucket=daily"

B) Tenant / org dimensions
7. workspace_id
8. workspace_name

9. project_id
   - Empty if filtered to "All projects" and backend returns cross-project rollup.

10. project_name

11. environment
   - One of: "prod", "staging", "dev", or empty if not applicable.

C) Time bucket
12. bucket
   - One of: "hour", "day" (v1)

13. bucket_start
   - ISO-8601 timestamp (inclusive)

14. bucket_end
   - ISO-8601 timestamp (exclusive)

D) Request / routing dimensions
15. api_route
   - Canonicalized route template.
   - Examples:
     - "/v1/chat/completions"
     - "/v1/embeddings"
     - "/v1/rerank"
     - "/v1/responses" (if OpenAI-compat layer)

16. api_route_raw_sample
   - Best-effort sample of an observed raw path for debugging (NOT guaranteed stable).
   - Empty if unavailable.
   - Example: "/v1/projects/123/chat/completions"

17. api_route_normalization_version
   - String id of normalization ruleset (ties to ADR / library version).
   - Example: "route_norm_v3"

18. deployment_mode
   - One of: "hosted", "dedicated", "private"

19. region
   - Cloud region code if applicable.
   - Example: "us-east-1", "eu-west-1".
   - Empty for on-prem private where region is not reported.

20. is_fallback
   - true if this row represents usage served by fallback routing policy (request did not use initially requested model).

21. fallback_reason
   - Empty unless is_fallback=true.
   - Examples: "capacity", "policy", "model_deprecated", "region_unavailable"

E) Model dimensions
22. model_id
   - Stable Redwood model identifier for serving.
   - Example: "llama-3.1-70b"

23. model_alias
   - Customer-facing alias if requested.
   - Example: "llama-3.1-70b-instruct"

24. model_family
   - Stable family for bucketing.
   - Example: "llama-3.1"

25. model_version
   - Serving version / build.
   - Example: "2026-01-28" or "v3.1.2" (string)

26. quantization_profile
   - Example: "fp16", "int8", "awq-int4". Empty if not applicable.

F) Usage volume
27. request_count
   - Total successful requests included in this bucket + dimension row.

28. error_count
   - Total requests that resulted in an error (4xx/5xx) and were billable per billing rules (see notes). This field is contentious; see “Open questions”.

29. retry_count
   - Total retry attempts attributed to this bucket/route/model.
   - IMPORTANT: retry_count counts additional attempts beyond the first attempt.

30. stream_count
   - Count of requests using streaming responses.

31. prompt_tokens
   - Total input tokens.

32. completion_tokens
   - Total output tokens.

33. total_tokens
   - prompt_tokens + completion_tokens (redundant convenience)

34. cache_hit_prompt_tokens
   - Prompt tokens served from prefix/KV cache (input-side).

35. cache_miss_prompt_tokens
   - Prompt tokens not served from cache.

36. cache_hit_rate_prompt_tokens
   - Decimal string with 6 digits after decimal.
   - Defined as cache_hit_prompt_tokens / NULLIF(prompt_tokens, 0)
   - Empty if prompt_tokens=0.

G) Latency (aggregated)
37. latency_ms_p50
38. latency_ms_p95
39. latency_ms_p99
   - Integers (milliseconds).
   - Empty if insufficient samples (e.g., <20 requests) depending on privacy/quality thresholds.

H) Cost + billing alignment
40. currency_code
   - "USD" (v1). Included for forward compatibility.

41. cost_prompt_usd
42. cost_completion_usd
43. cost_total_usd
   - Decimal string, fixed scale (see rounding rules).

44. unit_price_prompt_per_1k_tokens_usd
45. unit_price_completion_per_1k_tokens_usd
   - Decimal string. Empty if not applicable (e.g., flat-rate dedicated contract where marginal price not exposed).

46. pricing_plan
   - Example: "hosted-usage", "dedicated-reserved", "private-license"

47. billing_usage_meter
   - Internal-ish meter name for reconciliation.
   - Example: "chat_tokens", "embeddings_tokens"

48. billing_reconciliation_key
   - String allowing us to join back to billing exports without exposing invoice ids.
   - Proposed format: "ws:{workspace_id}|plan:{pricing_plan}|meter:{billing_usage_meter}|currency:{currency_code}"

---

6) Rounding + numeric formatting rules

Rationale
- Finance needs deterministic totals; Engineering needs accurate sums.
- We should never rely on Excel floating point interpretation.

Token counts
- Integers, no separators.
- prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, etc. MUST be whole numbers.

Latency
- Integers in milliseconds.

Costs and prices
- All currency numeric values formatted as decimal strings with fixed scale.

Scale
- cost_*_usd: 6 decimal places.
  - Example: "12.345678"
- unit_price_*: 6 decimal places.

Rounding method
- Round half up at the final aggregation step to 6 decimals.
- Avoid per-event rounding. Aggregate at higher precision internally (>= 1e-9) then round once per row.

Totals consistency note
- Console tables may show 2 decimals for readability; CSV uses 6 decimals.
- Billing/invoice exports may use 2 decimals at invoice line level; reconciliation tolerances should account for differences in timing boundaries + rounding (see ENG-3817).

---

7) Currency handling

v1 assumptions
- USD only.
- currency_code will always be "USD".

Future-proofing
- If we ever support non-USD invoicing, we should:
  - Keep cost_* columns in invoiced currency (currency_code)
  - Add parallel cost_*_usd columns OR add exchange_rate_to_usd and cost_total_usd.
- For now, do NOT emit exchange rates; will confuse customers if there is only USD.

---

8) Bucket selection rules (important for performance)

We auto-select bucket granularity based on time range unless explicitly set:
- <= 48h: hour buckets
- > 48h and <= 62d: day buckets
- > 62d: export may be rejected or forced to day buckets with warning (see limits).

Bucket boundaries
- Computed in export_time_zone (UTC in beta).
- bucket_start inclusive, bucket_end exclusive.

---

9) Dimension normalization rules (route + model)

Route
- api_route MUST be the canonical route template produced by the shared route normalization library (see ADR + ENG-3813).
- api_route_raw_sample is best-effort for debugging only.
- Cardinality guardrails:
  - If normalization fails or route is too high-cardinality, api_route should be set to "/unknown" and api_route_raw_sample populated.

Model
- model_id should be stable internal identifier.
- model_alias is what the user asked for (may be empty).
- model_family/model_version are used for bucketing and avoiding alias explosion.

Known sharp edge
- Alias collisions can produce duplicate-looking rows in BI tools if users group by model_alias instead of model_id/model_family.
- We should document recommended grouping keys (see section 13).

---

10) Limits & safety

Max rows
- Soft limit: 2,000,000 rows per export job.
- If estimated rows exceed limit, fail with actionable error (suggest narrower range or fewer group-by dimensions).

Max file size
- Soft limit: 1 GB uncompressed.

Async only
- Export is generated asynchronously and returned via signed download URL.

Retention
- Exports only available for download for 7 days (proposed). After that, URL expires.

Audit logging
- Every export generation + download should emit audit events (security requirement). CSV format does not include audit info; it is stored separately.

---

11) Examples

Example 1: Daily route+model rollup (hosted)

Example 2: Dedicated + fallback usage present
- Two rows can exist for same route+model_id if is_fallback differs, depending on how the request was served.

... api_route=/v1/chat/completions ... deployment_mode=dedicated ... is_fallback=false ... model_id=llama-3.1-70b ...
... api_route=/v1/chat/completions ... deployment_mode=dedicated ... is_fallback=true fallback_reason=capacity ... model_id=llama-3.1-8b ...

Example 3: Route normalization failure
- Route set to /unknown; raw sample populated.

... api_route=/unknown, api_route_raw_sample="/v1/users/abc123/chat/completions" ...

---

12) Recommended customer guidance (docs/tooltips)

If importing into a BI tool:
- Use model_id OR (model_family + model_version) as grouping keys.
- Treat model_alias as display-only.
- Prefer api_route over api_route_raw_sample.
- Summing cost_total_usd across rows should match the Console totals for the same filters/time range, within reconciliation tolerance (timing lag + late events).

---

13) Open questions / TODOs

1) error_count semantics
- Do we count only billable errors? Or all errors?
- Finance preference: billable-only.
- Support preference: all errors to debug spikes.
- Proposal: keep error_count as ALL errors; add billable_error_count later (append-only column). For beta, we can ship error_count=all and document it.

2) Dedicated pricing transparency
- For dedicated contracts, unit prices may be contract-specific and sensitive.
- Proposal: leave unit_price_* empty for dedicated/private, but still provide cost_total_usd if cost attribution is supported for chargeback. Confirm with Product/Security.

3) Latency privacy threshold
- If a row has low request_count, do we blank latency percentiles to avoid misleading stats?
- Proposal: blank latency_ms_* if request_count < 20.

4) Cache fields for non-chat routes
- For embeddings/rerank, cache_hit_prompt_tokens may be 0/empty depending on feature support.
- Keep columns present but values may be 0.

5) "Streaming overhead" cost
- We have a goal to reflect streaming overhead. Do we include it in cost_total_usd only, or break out a cost_streaming_overhead_usd column?
- Proposal: v1 does NOT add extra cost column; keep costs fully inclusive, and expose streaming via stream_count + completion_tokens (proxy). Add cost_streaming_overhead_usd later if we can attribute cleanly.

6) Consistency vs billing timeline
- Late events/backfill can cause small shifts day-over-day.
- Proposal: add data_freshness_timestamp to the export metadata (append-only column later) OR embed in export_filters string now. For v1, we currently only have export_generated_at.

---

14) Change log

2026-01-09 (Dylan): Initial skeleton, column brainstorm.
2026-01-18 (Nadia/Logan): Added cache hit/miss fields, fallback flags, reconciliation key.
2026-01-27 (Rishi): Fixed-scale decimals (6dp) and “round once” guidance.
2026-02-12 (Felix): Added latency percentiles + normalization version + raw sample field.
